entries.title: Psalms 73:1
segments:
The psalmist relates through what a severe inward conflict he has passed in view of the prosperity of the wicked and the afflictions of the righteous, and how he has overcome it by a revelation in God's sanctuary of the different ends that await the two classes of men. 
 
  To such as are of a clean heart; by these words he limits his declaration concerning Israel to such as are Israelites indeed.

entries.title: Psalms 73:3
segments: Envy is as the rottenness of the bones.  He who indulges in it, whether saint or sinner, will be wretched.

entries.title: Psalms 73:4
segments: No bands; no peculiar terrors or distresses.

entries.title: Psalms 73:5
segments: Not in trouble; as many pious men are.

entries.title: Psalms 73:6
segments: As a chain; that is, a chain worn for ornament.
The pride of the wicked is increased by their prosperity, which may be given them in wrath as a punishment for sins, and be the occasion of ripening them for ruin.

entries.title: Psalms 73:7
segments: More; of this world.

entries.title: Psalms 73:9
segments: Walketh through the earth; is used without restraint.

entries.title: Psalms 73:10
segments:
Therefore; because of this disagreement between the character of men and their present lot. 
 
  His people return hither; of this clause the original admits of two readings, and it is otherwise of difficult explanation.  Our English version follows one reading, the other is thus: "He maketh his people to return hither."  Of the various interpretations that have been proposed, the following is perhaps as probable as any: God makes his people, after all their wanderings this way and that in search of an explanation of this mystery, to come back hither, namely, to the point whence they set out--that good men are afflicted, and bad men prospered. 
 
  Waters of a full cup are wrung out to them; they drink to the dregs a bitter cup in witnessing the prosperity of the wicked, while they are themselves filled with trouble, and their sufferings are aggravated by the temptation to distrust God's justice. 
 
Great afflictions are no certain sign of peculiar wickedness; they may be sent in mercy, as fatherly chastisements, and be designed to wean men from the world, quicken them in duty, and fit them for heaven.

entries.title: Psalms 73:11
segments: They; the wicked.

entries.title: Psalms 73:13
segments: I have cleansed my heart in vain; this was what the psalmist was tempted to say, that his piety was useless.

entries.title: Psalms 73:14
segments: Plagued; visited with distresses.

entries.title: Psalms 73:15
segments: I should offend; such doctrines expressed would grieve the people of God, as being contrary to their experience, contrary to truth, and adapted to do mischief.

entries.title: Psalms 73:16
segments:
To know this; the reasons of the prosperity of the wicked and the adversity of the righteous. 
 
The ways of Providence with men often appear unaccountable, and the reasons of them will not be known in this world.  We must keep in view the end of the righteous and the wicked, and act with habitual reference to the closing scenes of life.

entries.title: Psalms 73:18
segments: In slippery places; where, notwithstanding their present prosperity, they are on the brink of perdition.

entries.title: Psalms 73:19
segments: Brought into desolation; perish at death.

entries.title: Psalms 73:20
segments: When thou awakest; when God leaves the wicked for a season to triumph over the good, he is said to sleep.
Their image; their vain show of happiness, which is as unsubstantial and fleeting as a night-vision.

entries.title: Psalms 73:21
segments: Thus my heart was grieved; before I understood the end of the wicked.  The psalmist reviews his former feelings with deep repentance.

entries.title: Psalms 73:22
segments: To envy the wicked on account of their worldly prosperity is foolish and sinful.  It is finding fault with the providence of God, and exposes those who indulge in it to his wrath.

entries.title: Psalms 73:23
segments:
Thou hast holden me; kept him from utter apostasy and ruin. 
 
God holds up his people and keeps them, notwithstanding their follies and sins; and in drawing near to him in humble repentance and obedient faith, they find not only their greatest safety, but also their highest joy.

entries.title: Psalms 73:24
segments:
Afterward; after the trials of the present life. 
 
  Receive me to glory; the consciousness of union by faith and love with the eternal God, brings to the psalmist the assurance of a blessed immortality to be spent in God's presence.

entries.title: Psalms 73:25
segments: But thee; none in comparison with God.

entries.title: Psalms 73:26
segments:
My flesh and my heart faileth; these words describe his mortal body as subject to decay and death. 
 
  Strength of my heart; the supporter of my soul.  He uses the word "heart" here of his spiritual and immortal nature.
